why: AHD and Wikipedia both define the reticulum as the second compartment of the ruminant stomach.
AHD, Wikipedia and WordNet (Vocabulary.com) define the omasum as the third compartment.
AHD and Wikipedia define the abomasum as the fourth compartment, the true (digesting) stomach.
RHS: quinces are not edible raw but are cooked into jelly and paste; AHD: used for jelly or cooked dishes.
Woodland Trust: rowan berries are edible when cooked (jam); Wikipedia: raw fruit bitter, parasorbic acid irritates the stomach; AHD: orange-red berries of Sorbus aucuparia.
Wikipedia: sloes are traditionally harvested after the first frosts; AHD and Woodland Trust: blue-black blackthorn fruit used for sloe gin and preserves.
Gymnosperm Database (130 spp., largest conifer genus) and Wikipedia (113–119 spp.) confirm Pinus as the largest genus; AHD notes needle fascicles.

Wikipedia (EN, DE) and giftpflanzen.com call monkshood the most poisonous plant in Europe; the superlative is a common attribution rather than a measured ranking, which the wording's "considered" covers.
AHD, the Natural History Museum and Wikipedia confirm ambergris from sperm-whale intestines as a perfume fixative.
GBIF backbone taxonomy and an ADW-listed paper place Proteus anguinus in the order Caudata (synonym Urodela, as Wikipedia gives it).
Bat Conservation International: bats belong to the order Chiroptera.
Australian Museum, AHD and Wikipedia: the platypus is a monotreme (order Monotremata), the egg-laying mammals.
Peer-reviewed literature uses "cold torpor" for the cold-induced immobility of ectotherms (reptiles), matching the German Kältestarre.
Wikipedia and AHD: Geranium is called cranesbill after its beak-like fruit capsule.
German Wikipedia: Hahnenfuß refers to the bird-foot-like leaves; AHD: crowfoot = Ranunculus.
changes: English wording now says "named in German after a bird's foot".

why: BMEL and the Bundeswaldinventur 2022: beech 17 % (2012: about 15 %), still the most common broadleaf species ahead of oak (12 %).
changes: Wording now names the 2012 and 2022 shares; reviewBy 2027-10-23.

why: The 2012 inventory lists spruce first among the commonest species and German Wikipedia confirms spruce led by area for decades until 2022.
The 2012 inventory order (Fichte, Kiefer, Buche, Eiche) puts the pine second; in 2022 it leads (BMEL).
Deutsches Ärzteblatt review (90 % of fatal mushroom poisonings), CDC MMWR and Wikipedia attribute most mushroom deaths to Amanita phalloides.
AHD and Wikipedia: commercial cork is the stripped bark (phellem) of the cork oak.
A peer-reviewed paper describes cotton fibres as single-celled seed trichomes; Wikipedia and AHD describe the fibre growing around the seeds.
AHD and Wikipedia define courtship as the animal behaviour leading to mating.
British Deer Society: the red deer breeding season, the rut, runs end of September to November with roaring stags; Wikipedia and WordNet concur.
Wikipedia and AHD: spawning is the release of eggs and sperm into the water by fish and amphibians.
Wikipedia: in birds moulting is the periodic replacement of feathers; AHD concurs.
Audubon and Wikipedia name the talon-locked tumble a cartwheel courtship display, while the Smithsonian National Zoo calls it a territorial fight, so the premise was softened.
changes: Wording now says "usually described as a courtship flight"; body notes the territorial interpretation.

why: Amateur Entomologists' Society, Wikipedia and AHD: head, thorax and abdomen.
AES and Wikipedia: complete metamorphosis runs egg, larva, pupa, adult.
Wikipedia: houseflies rub their legs together to clean them so the tarsal chemoreceptors taste afresh; a peer-reviewed review lists cleaning sensory organs as a function of insect grooming.
CDC calls the mosquito the world's deadliest animal; WHO counts >700,000 vector-borne deaths a year (malaria 610,000 in 2024), so the "over a million" premise was replaced.
changes: Wording and body: "hundreds of thousands" instead of "over a million".

why: A peer-reviewed paper defines feralization as domestic animals becoming established without human propagation; AHD and Wikipedia define feral as returned from domestication.
AHD and Wikipedia define inbreeding as mating of closely related individuals.
Dictionary.com, Dog Breed Info and Wikipedia: a schnoodle is a miniature schnauzer × poodle cross.
AHD (etymology from Corinth) and Wikipedia (Black Corinth grape): the currant is a small seedless raisin named after Corinth.
The poem text ("Am Brunnen vor dem Tore / Da steht ein Lindenbaum") and German Wikipedia (original title Der Lindenbaum).
Wikipedia: the almond fruit is a drupe, not a true nut; a 2025 meta-analysis: almond consumption lowers LDL-C; AHD: native to Asia.
NOAA and Wikipedia: toothed whales and dolphins echolocate to locate prey; echolocation is not their communication channel.
changes: Wording narrowed to toothed whales and dolphins hunting and finding their way (card kept in cardText).

why: The Gymnosperm Database places the General Sherman tree in Sequoia National Park, as do NPS and Wikipedia; age estimates (2,100–2,700) differed from the card's 1,900–2,500.
changes: Age premise now "more than 2,000 years" in wording and body; card kept in cardText; notes record the card figure.

why: A peer-reviewed paper (116.07 m, Redwood National Park) and Wikipedia confirm Hyperion stands in Redwood National Park.
